text.p: Following are the main stories in Tuesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Malaysia's Securities Commission has urged the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange to set up an independent unit to enforce compliance standards. The compliance officers would monitor trading and operational activities of trading firms.

-- The Malaysian cabinet has ordered suspension of all projects involved in cutting of trees and hills. The projects will be reviewed and those not seen environment-friendly will be shelved and disciplinary action will be taken against officers who have approved those projects.
-- Malaysian Airline System will begin test flights to the new Kuala Lumpur International Airport from September. The $3.6 billion airport is due to open next year.
-- The Rating Agency Malaysia Bhd said it expected Malaysia's economic growth to consolidate. It forecast gross domestic product growth in 1997 at 8.3 percent and 7.5 to 8.0 percent in 1998.

-- The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange was among the three worst performers among emerging markets in April, according to Morgan Stanley Capital International. Southeast Asian markets trailed all others with the Philippines falling 17 percent and Malaysia down 11.3 percent.
